samples.text: The service is running on a temporary basis, not a repaired one: manual agency code mapping override applied to complete valuation for the period. That override was needed because the confirmed cause is stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register, and correcting the register properly requires decisions about code ownership that cannot be taken inside the incident. Compared with normal operation, the difference is that a person, not the reference data, now decides how each affected legacy code translates. The override covers this period only and has been checked against the records it touched, but it has not been through the review that a permanent mapping change would need. Anyone deciding whether to wait can rely on the current output for this period, because the override has completed the valuation. Nobody should assume the next run will behave the same way. Until the register itself is corrected, each new run will need the same manual step, and the incident should stay open on that basis. Waiting for

The valuation failure was caused by stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register. Legacy agency codes and cloud agency codes are both live and do not translate one to one, so a mapping row that has fallen out of date sends the inventory valuation service to the wrong reference entry without raising an error. At first the cause was recorded as overnight ERP outage, a reasonable guess because the valuation run sits inside the overnight batch window. That explanation was set aside on evidence rather than opinion: ERP logs show no interruption during the valuation window. Once the outage theory was gone, the only input that had changed between a good run and a bad one was the mapping data itself. The formal classification records the deeper problem as control failure: the mapping table has no registered owner and no required reviewer, which is why the stale row was never caught before it reached production.
